analysis.title: Americas Energy Services: Updating Select Estimates Post-Earnings; Prefer PWR/MTZ for T&D Exposure and Risk/Reward
key_insights: GS updates estimates for specialty contractors (PWR, MTZ, MYRG, AGX) and behind-the-meter players (LBRT, PUMP, AESI) after earnings, and lowers price targets on most names given higher uncertainty over power and grid investment post midterm elections.
GS prefers PWR and MTZ, citing a structural need for US grid investment that creates durable growth beyond 2030.

PWR (Buy, PT $781 maintained): sees T&D as the main earnings driver, ~17% y/y Electric revenue growth in 2027, with 765 kV lines contributing from 2028. Estimates 2027 total revenue growth ~16% and EBITDA margin 11%.
PWR's MEP business supporting data centers is ~15-20% of revenue. GS sees margin expansion from pre-fabrication and better visibility from the integrated utility-style structure with hyperscalers.
PWR NTM EV/EBITDA multiple cut to 23.5x from 26.0x to reflect AI and power exposed market multiples. EBITDA estimates raised 7%/6%/4% for 2026/27/28.

MTZ (Buy, PT cut to $242 from $274): sees attractive risk/reward after underperformance, with current levels discounting regulatory and execution risks. Moderating Communications revenue, but expects benefit from BEAD and fiber, plus Power Delivery and Superior integration.
MTZ multiple cut to 11.0x from 12.0x on higher cost of capital from project push-outs. MTZ has high earnings exposure to non-data center work, which GS sees as differentiated growth.

MYRG (Neutral, PT $321 from $331): higher line-of-sight for T&D and C&I in 2027. C&I margin guided toward upper end of 6-9% range for 2027, with larger T&D projects starting in 2H27. EBITDA estimates raised 11%/12%/11%, multiple cut to 11.5x from 13.0x.
AGX (Buy, PT $407 from $565): estimates adjusted for timing of gas project awards, with NTM EV/EBITDA multiple cut to 20.5x from 29.0x. FY27 EBITDA unchanged, FY28/29 down 2%/1%.

Behind-the-meter OFS names show improving upside amid a broad power stock sell-off, but capital timing, site selection and post-midterm regulatory uncertainty remain risks. LBRT and AESI progressed toward securing ESAs, but formal project announcements are still awaited.
LBRT (Neutral, PT $16 from $23): EBITDA cut 3%/17%/12% for 2026/27/28 on North America and pressure pumping profitability amid Middle East disruptions. Through-cycle multiple cut to 4.0x from 4.25x.
AESI (Sell, PT $6 from $11): EBITDA cut 12%/14% for 2026/27 and raised 4% for 2028 on North America activity. Through-cycle multiple cut to 4.0x from 4.5x on downside risk to consensus.
PUMP (Neutral, PT $9 from $11): GS sees near-term value support from existing contracted MWs with a tangible path to earnings and cash flow. EBITDA raised 4%/6%/0%.
